start.lead: Grade scanned exam papers one question at a time, then make a report for every student.
start.new_hint: You will need your scanned papers. CAM2 guides you through five steps:
start.folder_missing: Folder not found. Plug in the USB stick or wait for OneDrive, or browse for it.
start.guide_lead: There is nothing to set up in CAM2 before the exam. Give the exam as usual, then scan the papers to PDF.
guide.1.title: Scan the whole class in one go
guide.1.text: Put the whole stack in the copier’s feeder and scan it to one PDF. CAM2 cuts it into each student’s paper, which saves time at the copier. The papers don’t need to be in class-list order.
guide.2.title: Too many sheets for the feeder? Scan in batches
guide.2.text: Most feeders take 50–100 sheets. Scan in batches and CAM2 joins the PDFs.
guide.3.title: Take the staples out
guide.3.text: Loose sheets go through the feeder. It is much quicker than scanning page by page on the glass.
guide.4.title: Booklets printed on A3
guide.4.text: Take the staples out and keep each student’s sheets together. Scan the whole class at A3, 2-sided. CAM2 unfolds each booklet and puts the pages in order. Don’t cut along the fold.
guide.5.title: Sheets upside down or in the wrong order?
guide.5.text: You can fix them in CAM2 when you check the scans.
guide.6.title: Scanner settings
guide.6.text: PDF, 200–300 dpi, 2-sided if the papers are printed on both sides. Greyscale scans are clearer.
guide.7.title: Using photos
guide.7.text: Use a scanning app on your phone. It straightens each page automatically.
guide.8.title: Students who sit the exam later
guide.8.text: Their papers can be added at any time, even after grading has started.
guide.9.title: The quickest set-up for next time
guide.9.text: Make question booklets plus separate answer sheets. Scan only the answer sheets.

step.4.hint: Grade one question at a time
step.5.hint: Check totals and make the student reports

save.not_saved_banner: Not saved — your work is kept safe on this computer. Reconnect the folder and click Save.

step1.title: Start a new grading session
step1.coach: Name the exam, choose the scanned papers, and choose where CAM2 should save your work.
step1.folder_hint: One PDF or picture per student
step1.combined_hint: From the photocopier, in one go or in batches
step1.paste_path: Or paste the path of a folder or PDF
step1.photos_hint: A folder with one picture per page, in order
step1.photos_found: {count} pictures found ({pages} pages), taken in file-name order.
step1.pdf_total: {files} PDFs, {pages} pages in all, joined in this order.
step1.layout: How is each paper laid out?
step1.layout_pages_hint: Loose or stapled sheets, answer sheets
step1.layout_booklet_hint: Two pages side by side on each scanned page (e.g. an A4 booklet on A3)
step1.layout_landscape_hint: These pages are landscape. If they are booklets scanned open, choose “Folded booklet”.
step1.booklet_pages: How many pages are in the booklet?
step1.booklet_inside_first: Inside sheets first (booklets were opened and stacked as they lay)
step1.booklet_fronts: Front sides come out upside down
step1.booklet_backs: Back sides come out upside down
step1.booklet_flip_hint: Check the preview. If every paper has pages upside down or out of order, tick a box. A single booklet or sheet that went in the wrong way can be fixed after importing.
step1.pages_per_student: How many pages is one student’s paper?
step1.class_size: How many students? (optional, to check for missing pages)
step1.split_class_ok: → {students} students. That matches the number of pages.
step1.split_missing: {students} students × {per} pages should be {expected} pages, but the PDF has {pages}: {n} page(s) missing. Papers after a missing page will be cut in the wrong place — check the thumbnails next.
step1.split_extra: {students} students × {per} pages should be {expected} pages, but the PDF has {pages}: {n} page(s) too many (a page may have gone through the scanner twice). Check the thumbnails next.
step1.split_leftover: → {students} students, but the last one has only {left} page(s). A page may be missing or extra somewhere — check the thumbnails next.
step1.paper_hint: The size the exam was printed on. CAM2 has guessed it from the scans where it could.
step1.save_folder: Where should this session be saved?
step1.save_folder_hint: Everything for this exam — scans, grades and reports — goes into this one folder. It can be on your computer, a USB stick or any cloud drive folder.*
step1.save_folder_cloud_note: * Cloud folders can take a while to sync. Let syncing finish before opening this session on another computer.
step1.create: Create session & bring in the scans →
step1.importing_note: Copying the papers into your session folder and making thumbnails.
step1.check_coach: Here is page 1 of all {count} papers. Check that each one looks like the front of a paper. Click a picture to see all its pages.
step1.no_students: No papers have been brought in yet.
step1.warn_leftover: The combined PDF did not divide evenly: the last paper has only {left} page(s).
step1.warn_class_missing: You expected {students} students ({expected} pages), but the PDF has {pages}: {n} page(s) missing.
step1.warn_class_extra: You expected {students} students ({expected} pages), but the PDF has {pages}: {n} page(s) too many.
step1.warn_advice: If a page is missing or extra, the papers after it are cut in the wrong place. Click the first wrong paper to fix its pages (remove the extra page, or add a blank one for the missing page), or re-scan from that paper and choose the scans again.
step1.choose_again_hint: The new scans replace the old ones. Your set-up is kept, but the papers will need slicing again.
step1.add_papers_hint: For example a student who sat the exam late. The new papers go after the others. Your set-up, names and grades are kept, and the new papers are ready to grade straight away.
pages.stream_note: These papers were cut from one long stack. Removing or adding a page shifts the pages of every paper after this one, and moving the first or last page swaps it with the paper next to it.
pages.swap_sheet: ⇄ This sheet’s front and back are swapped
pages.reverse_sheets: ⇅ This booklet’s sheets are in reverse order
pages.sheet_note: Page {page} is on sheet {sheet} of this booklet. The first two buttons fix that whole sheet (four pages).
pages.locked: This paper already has grades or comments, so its pages can no longer be changed.
pages.remove_message: Use this for a page that went through the scanner twice, or an empty page. The page can only be brought back by choosing the scans again.
step2.mode.title: How will you grade this exam?
step2.mode.coach: Choose one. You can change it later.
step2.mode.marks_hint: Each question is worth points (e.g. Q1 = 3 marks). Totals are added up for you.
step2.mode.rubric_hint: Each question gets a level from your rubric (e.g. 0–8). Averages are worked out for you.
step2.rubric.title: Your rubric
step2.rubric.coach: Type or paste your rubric’s levels and descriptors, or upload an Excel file. Change the levels to suit you — they don’t have to be 0–8.
step2.rubric.name: Criterion / rubric name
step2.rubric.descriptor_placeholder: What a student at this level can do…
step2.boxes.old_grid: This exam uses the older, coarser grid.
step2.boxes.coach_name: Drag a box around where students write their name (usually on page 1). Leave space around it — names often run past the line.
step2.boxes.coach_question: Drag a box around {label}: the question and its whole answer space.
step2.boxes.coach_add: Now drag the extra box for {label}. Use the page arrows if it is on another page.
step2.boxes.tip_space: Be generous. Leave room on every side for crossed-out work and answers that run outside the printed box.
step2.boxes.tip_question: Include the question text, so you can see what was asked while you grade.
step2.boxes.tip_parts: Question text somewhere else, such as one stem for parts a, b and c? Box it first, then use + Add another box for the answer.
step2.boxes.tip_overlap: Boxes may overlap the next question. That’s fine.
step2.boxes.label: Question label
step2.boxes.which_rubric_hint: Tick every criterion this question is assessed on. Each one gets its own level.
step2.boxes.add_box: + Add another box (answer or question text elsewhere)
step2.boxes.bad_range: That range does not fit this grid. Try something like A4:J10.
step2.boxes.check_hint: The same box on three other students’ papers. If writing is cut off at an edge, make the box bigger.
step2.boxes.name_done: ✓ Save name box & go to the questions →
step2.boxes.skip_name: Skip — there is no name box
step2.boxes.draw_first: Drag a box on the page first.
step2.boxes.order_hint: Click a question, then ↑ ↓ to move it. Grading and reports follow this order.
step2.boxes.new_or_move_title: A new question, or move the box?
step2.boxes.new_or_move: This box is in a different place from the box for {label}. What would you like to do?
step2.boxes.change_grid_confirm: The boxes you have drawn will be cleared, because they no longer fit the new grid. Labels, marks and rubrics are kept.
step2.choice.title: Choice questions
step2.choice.coach: Do students choose which questions to answer (for example, “answer 2 of 3”)?
step2.choice.tick: Tick the questions students choose between:
step2.slice.title: Slice the papers
step2.slice.coach: CAM2 will cut out every answer from every paper: {questions} question(s) × {students} student(s).
step2.slice.name_box_yes: The name box will be cut out too, to help you match names.
step2.slice.name_box_no: There is no name box; you will match names using page 1.
step2.slice.question: Question
step2.slice.working_note: This can take a minute for a big class.
step3.title: Match names
step3.coach: Pair each paper with a student. The picture shows what the student wrote in the name box.
step3.coach_no_name_box: Pair each paper with a student, using page 1 of each paper.
step3.list_hint: With a class list you pick names from a list instead of typing them.
step3.paste_help: Paste names one per line, for example straight from Excel.
step3.remove_list_confirm: Remove the class list and all matches made from it?
step3.pick_coach: Click the column with the names. If family and given names are in separate columns, click both, family name first.
step3.has_header: The first row is a heading, not a student
step3.rows_total: {n} rows in the file. Only the first few are shown.
step3.unmatched_confirm: {n} paper(s) have no name yet. You can continue and match them later.
step4.question: Question
step4.whole_page_hint: The red box shows where this answer was cut from. You can still grade on the right.
step4.last_paper: This is the last paper for this question.
step4.everything_done: Every question on every paper has a grade.
step4.show_all_hint: To look at graded papers again, untick “Show ungraded only”.
step5.title: Review & export
step5.coach_marks: Check every student. Click any mark to change it, or an amber “?” to grade it. “Total on report” changes only that student’s PDF — the calculated total is always kept.
step5.coach_rubric: Check every student. Click any level to change it, or an amber “?” to grade it. The final level starts as the average rounded half up; change it to your own judgement — CAM2 keeps the calculated average too.
step5.click_to_grade: Not graded yet — click to grade
step5.comment_legend: Has a comment — point at the grade to read it.
step5.incomplete_confirm: {n} student(s) still have ungraded questions. Their reports will show “Not graded”. Make the reports anyway?
step5.export_hint: CAM2 makes one PDF per student (named after the student, ready to email) and an Excel gradebook, all in the “reports” folder of this session. Making them again replaces the old ones.
step5.working_note: One PDF per student. This can take a minute for a big class.
step5.done_all: Done: {n} student PDFs and the Excel gradebook.
report.not_counted_long: Not counted: you answered more of the choice questions than needed, so your best answers were counted.
